title: Agent World Model: Infinity Synthetic Environments for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
one_liner: Train tool-using agents in many executable synthetic worlds so they can practice broadly without depending on one narrow benchmark environment.
lead: Training an agent needs many episodes, many task types, and reliable feedback. Real environments are expensive to build and slow to run. Fully language-simulated worlds can be fast, but their state changes may be inconsistent because the world update itself is just another generated response. This paper builds a large collection of code-driven synthetic environments backed by databases so that agents can practice across many tasks while still getting stable state transitions and dependable reward signals.

problem.h2: Agent training stalls when environments are too few, too slow, or too inconsistent
paras: A strong tool-using agent needs practice across many tasks, not just one benchmark setting. But collecting that practice from real or highly detailed environments is expensive, and fully generated environments may produce unstable world updates that weaken the reward signal.

The result is a scaling problem. Training cannot expand smoothly if every new environment is costly to author, costly to run, or too inconsistent to trust. The paper asks whether a large bank of executable synthetic worlds can provide diversity, speed, and stable feedback at the same time.

callout.b: The paper's move in one sentence.
callout.html: Generate many code-driven synthetic environments with database-backed state so agents can train broadly because executable worlds make transitions and reward easier to trust.

panels.title: 1. Training wants many worlds
panels.viz_args: Agents need varied tasks, tool sets, and observations.
panels.caption: Narrow practice leads to narrow behavior because the policy only sees a small slice of possible interactions.

panels.title: 2. Real environments are expensive
panels.viz_args: Building and running detailed worlds takes time and engineering effort.
panels.caption: That makes large-scale reinforcement learning hard because data collection becomes the bottleneck.

panels.title: 3. Synthetic worlds are generated
panels.caption: The paper builds many code-driven worlds so the agent can practice at larger scale.

panels.title: 4. State updates are executable
panels.viz_args: World changes are handled by code and databases, not by free-form narration.
panels.caption: That helps reward stay dependable because the environment follows explicit rules.

panels.title: 5. Training transfers outward
panels.viz_args: Agents trained in synthetic worlds are tested on separate benchmarks.
panels.caption: The key question is whether broad synthetic practice produces generalization beyond the training worlds.

steps.text: Create a large set of everyday synthetic worlds with tasks, tools, and observations so that agent training is not tied to one benchmark.

steps.b: Back each world with executable state
steps.text: Use code and databases to update the world because explicit state transitions are easier to trust than free-form simulation text.

steps.b: Train agents across the world bank
steps.text: Run multi-turn reinforcement learning episodes over many synthetic tasks so that the policy sees broader interaction patterns.
Use direct access to world state when scoring episodes so that reward reflects actual task progress instead of uncertain textual interpretation.
Test on separate benchmarks so that the result shows whether synthetic practice transfers beyond the generated environment bank.

paras: The paper changes the source of agent experience. Instead of learning mainly from benchmark-specific worlds, the policy learns from a large reusable library of synthetic executable environments.
object.object: the environment source feeding agent reinforcement learning

hidden.name: how much useful general practice the agent gets per unit of environment cost
paras: The hidden quantity is not just the number of training episodes. It is the amount of useful, trustworthy, diverse practice the agent receives for the environment-building cost paid.

A world bank is valuable only if those episodes teach skills that transfer outward. Code-driven state and database-backed records help because they make transitions and rewards stable, while large world variety helps because repeated exposure to different task structures discourages narrow benchmark habits.

heat.caption: The method cares most about variety plus reliable state, because broad practice is useful only when the world updates and rewards can be trusted.

reads.html: The real question is how much broadly useful practice you get for the money and engineering time spent building worlds.
Executable synthetic worlds improve training scale by combining diversity with dependable transitions, which means reinforcement learning can collect broader and cleaner experience.

mechanism.h2: Why executable synthetic worlds can train useful policies
paras: Synthetic worlds can scale because they are cheaper to create and run than many fully realistic environments. That alone is not enough, though. If world transitions are inconsistent, the policy learns from noise. The paper's code-driven design matters because the next state follows explicit program logic and stored data rather than an unconstrained textual guess.

The environment bank also helps transfer because the agent sees many combinations of tasks, tools, and observations. That variety reduces overfitting to one benchmark path and encourages general problem-solving habits that can be reused elsewhere.

stages.s: World templates plus task and tool definitions
Generate many executable synthetic worlds with stored state
Train agents with direct reward from true world state
Policies that can generalize beyond one world bank

math.words: Useful training supply can be viewed as environment variety times state reliability, because many episodes help only when those episodes come from worlds whose updates can be trusted.
symbols: amount of broadly useful agent practice available for learning
range of different tasks, tools, and situations covered by the world bank
how consistently world updates and rewards reflect the true task state

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Suppose one world bank covers many task types, giving world variety 8.
Suppose its executable updates are highly consistent, giving state reliability 9.
Then training supply is 72 by this simple product view.
A second bank with the same variety but unreliable updates might score only 40.
That lower value reflects a practical truth: broad practice loses value when the world itself cannot be trusted.

math.note: The paper's full setup is larger than this summary, but the equation captures the main scaling claim about diversity and reliability together.

bars.h2: What the experiments are trying to show

charts.title: Narrow benchmark-specific training
charts.note: A narrow environment can still teach something, but it often transfers poorly because the policy sees too few situations.

charts.title: Large synthetic world bank
charts.note: The desired result is broader transfer because the agent practiced across many executable environments instead of one narrow training setting.

items.b: Synthetic worlds can still miss real deployment quirks.
items.html: Even a large world bank may omit important real-world irregularities, so transfer can stall because the training data mix still leaves out decisive edge cases.
If many worlds are built from similar templates, the agent may learn the template rather than the broader skill because superficial variety hides structural repetition.

items.b: Reward design can still be narrow.
items.html: Direct state access helps scoring, but a poorly chosen reward can still teach the wrong lesson because reliable measurement does not guarantee the right objective.
The approach is strongest when the world bank is both varied and executable, because that combination gives reinforcement learning many trustworthy practice episodes.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a small bank of executable household task environments with stored state and tool interfaces. Train one agent only on a single benchmark environment and another on the synthetic bank. Keep the reward tied to true world state rather than text-only judgments.

The demo should then evaluate both agents on held-out environments with related but not identical tasks. The synthetic-bank agent should transfer better because it has already practiced across a wider range of situations.
demo.metric_eq: transfer_gain = heldout_success_bank - heldout_success_single ; supply_gain = training_supply_bank - training_supply_single
demo.closing: The point of the demo is to show that many executable synthetic worlds help because they supply diverse and dependable practice at training time.
